register: wave-10 authoring register (S-B10 tranche) — part 2 of 2

items.stem: In most condensation polymerisations, what is the formula of the small molecule that is released?
items.modelAnswer: The small molecule is H2O — water.

items.stem: State the difference between the product lists of addition and condensation polymerisation.
items.misconceptionClass: polymer only versus polymer plus small molecule
items.modelAnswer: Addition polymerisation forms the polymer molecule only, while condensation also releases a small molecule such as water.

items.stem: Explain why each condensation monomer must carry a functional group at both ends of its molecule.
items.modelAnswer: A group at each end lets one monomer link to the next monomer on either side, so the chain can keep growing in both directions.

items.stem: State how many water molecules form for each ester linkage made, and hence how many were released for a chain with 150 ester linkages.
items.modelAnswer: One water molecule forms for every ester linkage made, so 150 ester linkages release 150 water molecules.

items.stem: State the functional group carried at both ends of a dicarboxylic acid monomer.
items.modelAnswer: A dicarboxylic acid carries a COOH group at either end.

items.stem: What name is given to a monomer that carries an OH group at both of its ends?
items.modelAnswer: Such a monomer is a diol.

items.stem: Explain why making a polyester from a dicarboxylic acid and a diol releases exactly one water molecule per ester link formed.
items.misconceptionClass: one COOH plus one OH per link
items.modelAnswer: Each COOH group reacts with one OH group, and that single pairing releases one water as the ester link closes.

items.stem: A polyester is boiled with water and breaks back into its two monomers. State the name of this reverse process and the small molecule it consumes.
items.modelAnswer: The process is hydrolysis — water is added back to break the ester links into the monomers.

items.stem: Name the two feedstocks from which micro-organisms build biopolyesters.
items.modelAnswer: Biopolyesters are synthesised from sugars and plant oils.

items.stem: List the three functional group types found along a biopolyester chain.
items.modelAnswer: The chains contain ester, amide and ether functional groups.

items.stem: Explain why a biopolyester breaks down in the environment while an ordinary addition polymer does not.
items.modelAnswer: The ester, amide and ether groups along the biopolyester chain give it its biodegradable character, which addition polymers lack because their carbon-carbon backbone is inert.

items.stem: A supermarket wants packaging that composts after use. State which family of polymers meets this requirement and what happens to it in the ground.
items.modelAnswer: Biopolyesters meet the requirement — they biodegrade naturally in the environment once their job is done.

items.stem: State the word that describes an addition polymer's chemical unreactiveness.
items.modelAnswer: The polymer is described as inert.

items.stem: Name the elements joined by the strong bonds that run along an addition polymer's backbone.
items.modelAnswer: The backbone bonds join carbon atoms to carbon atoms — strong carbon-carbon bonds.

items.stem: Explain why a plastic bottle made of an addition polymer can persist in soil for decades.
items.modelAnswer: Decomposers cannot break the polymer down because its strong carbon-carbon bonds make it inert, so it cannot biodegrade.

items.stem: A council considers shipping its plastic waste to a bigger landfill. State the long-term land consequence that makes this a temporary fix only.
items.modelAnswer: Landfill disposal takes up valuable land and the sites fill up quickly, so a bigger site only delays the same problem.

items.stem: State the greenhouse gas released when polymers are burned.
items.modelAnswer: Burning polymers releases carbon dioxide, a greenhouse gas.

items.stem: Name the toxic gas released when PVC is incinerated.
items.modelAnswer: Hydrogen chloride is released when polymers containing chlorine, such as PVC, are burned.

items.stem: Explain why a build-up of carbon monoxide from an incinerator is dangerous to people nearby.
items.modelAnswer: Carbon monoxide is toxic because it reduces the blood's capacity to carry oxygen around the body.

items.stem: A waste plant burns mixed polymer waste and uses the heat to warm nearby greenhouses. State the energy benefit being exploited and one toxic product that incomplete burning adds to the emissions.
items.modelAnswer: Burning polymers releases a lot of heat energy, which warms the greenhouses; incomplete combustion also produces toxic carbon monoxide.

items.stem: State the reagent that adds across the ethene double bond in industrial ethanol production.
items.modelAnswer: Steam adds across the ethene double bond.

items.stem: Give the two operating numbers — temperature and pressure — for the industrial hydration of ethene.
items.modelAnswer: The plant runs at about 300 degrees Celsius and 60 to 70 atmospheres of pressure.

items.stem: Explain why unreacted ethene can be drawn off from the top of the chamber while the liquids stay behind.
items.misconceptionClass: ethene boils far below the liquids
items.modelAnswer: Ethene boils at minus 103 degrees Celsius, far below the boiling points of ethanol and water, so it leaves as a gas while the liquids remain.

items.stem: An oil refinery cracks long molecules before the ethene is hydrated. State the family of feedstock that cracking starts from and name the product stream used here.
items.modelAnswer: Cracking starts from long-chain hydrocarbons and produces the ethene feedstock that the hydration plant uses.

items.stem: Write the equation, with formulae, for the fermentation of glucose.
items.modelAnswer: C6H12O6 gives 2CO2 plus 2C2H5OH — glucose breaks into carbon dioxide and ethanol.

items.stem: State the optimum temperature for yeast in fermentation and the window around it.
items.modelAnswer: Yeast works best at about 30 degrees Celsius, inside a 25 to 35 degree window.

items.stem: Explain why the fermentation vessel is sealed from the air.
items.modelAnswer: Air is excluded because the yeast must respire without oxygen to make ethanol — the ethanol-forming route is anaerobic.

items.stem: A brewer's vat stops producing ethanol at about 15 percent alcohol even though sugar remains. State the cause and the operating consequence for the plant.
items.modelAnswer: The yeast has died — yeast dies once the alcohol reaches about 15 percent, so the route runs in batches rather than continuously.
